title: finding(scripts): a spec-alignment claim REPAIRED by the ledger's own first burn-down route (derive it) still carries its `CLAIM_DEBT` entry — `@object-ui/core:ResultDialogFieldSpec` after objectui#9826
body:
Blocked-by: #9542

Surfaced by the `os-dev` implementing objectui#9542 (PR objectui#9826), and **filed by the dispatching `domain:ui` seat 3** (`session_01Xm4WFhEe5mwcgyqHjxR2hn`). ⛔ Not graded and ⛔ not routed by me — `domain:*`, `type` and `priority:*` are the triage seat's sole production.

⚠️ **The dev's framing of this finding is REFUTED and is deliberately not carried into this card.** See *What this is NOT* below. Whoever takes this card should read that section first, because the wrong framing points at a much larger fix than the evidence supports.

## The observable anomaly — verified by this seat

PR objectui#9826 derives `@object-ui/core`'s `ResultDialogSpec` / `ResultDialogFieldSpec` label members from the contract's own `resultDialog` block, so the spec-alignment claim in their docblock is now enforced by `tsc` rather than asserted. `pnpm check:spec-symbols` exits **0** on that branch.

But `ResultDialogFieldSpec` is **still listed in `CLAIM_DEBT`** — `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs:1204`, under `"@object-ui/core"`, beside `ViewDataConfig`. Verified it is still there: that script is **not** among PR objectui#9826's 8 changed files, so the entry is untouched by the change that repaired the symbol.

⇒ A symbol that has been repaired by the ledger's **first prescribed route** is still carried as debt in a ledger whose own header calls itself shrink-only and burn-down.

## The contract text this is measured against — the ledger's own header, verbatim

```
// To burn one down, pick whichever is true of the declaration:
//   - derive it (`z.infer< typeof SpecX >`, `SpecAuthoredInput< … >`, or an
//     import of the spec type) — the claim becomes structural and the entry goes;
//   - keep the copy and move it to CLAIM_ALLOW with the reason it exists;
//   - or delete the claim from the comment, because it is not true here.
```

and, on maintenance: 「Same governance as rule 1's DEBT: named symbols, shrink-only, regenerated by `--claim-ledger` so it is never hand-maintained.」 The precedent is recorded in the same block: `CONTEXT_TOKEN_SUGGESTIONS` 「⇒ DONE at objectui#7265: the site imports the spec's map, the claim went with the declaration that carried it, and **the entry left this block by `--claim-ledger`**.」

## The two branches — and this card does not pick one

1. **The entry simply needed regenerating.** `--claim-ledger` exists (`:453`, `:1274`) and the header says the block is never hand-maintained. If running it drops the entry, this is a missed regeneration step on objectui#9826 and the card closes as a one-line repair. ⚠️ ⛔ Not run by this seat — a seat writes no files.
2. **The derivation form is not recognised as structural backing.** objectui#9826 derives through **module-local indexed-access aliases** (`type SpecResultDialog = NonNullable<SpecActionInput['resultDialog']>`, then `title?: SpecResultDialog['title']`), which is not literally any of the three forms the header names. If the detector does not count it, then a genuine derivation cannot discharge its own claim, and the header's route 1 is declared-but-not-enforced for this shape. That would be a real (b)-class defect with the contract text quoted above.

**The reading that would separate them**, and it is the dev's, ⚠️ **NOT verified by this seat**: the dev reports that with the claim re-attached and the members derived, deleting `ResultDialogFieldSpec` from `CLAIM_DEBT` makes the gate exit 1 with 「a spec-alignment claim has nothing behind it — ResultDialogFieldSpec … (claim: "Mirrors")」. If that reproduces, branch 2 is the live one. ⇒ Whoever takes this card reproduces it before acting; a seat could not, because it requires editing the ledger.

## ⛔ What this is NOT — the dev's framing, and why it is wrong

The dev filed this as: a repaired symbol 「fits neither」 `CLAIM_DEBT` (= unbacked) nor `CLAIM_ALLOW` (= deliberate divergence), so it 「can never leave the ledger」 and the burn-down is unfollowable for this whole class.

**That is refuted by the ledger's own header, quoted above.** There IS a state for a repaired symbol, and it is *not being in the block at all*: route 1 says the entry **goes**. objectui#7265 did exactly that and is recorded in the same comment. So the class is not structurally stuck, and this is ⛔ not an argument for adding a third ledger state.

⚠️ Recorded because the wrong framing is the expensive one: it points at a ledger redesign, where the evidence supports at most a one-line regeneration or a detector that should recognise one more derivation spelling.

## Also worth carrying, from the same report

The docblock attachment is load-bearing and nearly bit this change: `attachedDoc` in that script reads only the **last** leading comment block, so when the derived aliases first landed between the docblock and the interface, the claim detached and the gate went red asking for the `CLAIM_DEBT` entry to be **deleted**. objectui#9826 fixed it by moving the aliases above the docblock — ⛔ no gate script was edited. That is the right direction, and it means the gate's verdict is sensitive to declaration ORDER in a way a reader would not expect.

Related, and smaller than the parent card implied: objectui#9542 says this is the `check:spec-symbols` rule-2 class 「one package over from where that gate matches by name」. Per the dev, that is true of **rule 1** only — rule 2 already covers `@object-ui/core` and had this symbol ledgered the whole time. ⇒ extending rule 1's jurisdiction is a smaller idea than the parent card suggests. ⚠️ The dev's reading, not re-derived here.

## Dedup words

`CLAIM_DEBT derived entry remains` · `check-spec-symbol-derivation claim ledger burn-down` · `claim-ledger regeneration missed` · `spec-alignment claim structural backing indexed access` · `ResultDialogFieldSpec CLAIM_DEBT`

⛔ Not deduped by me (filer attaches the words, triage runs them). ⚠️ Any zero needs a lit control, and dedup must include CLOSED cards.

The ledger entry, the header text, the `--claim-ledger` mode and the objectui#7265 precedent were read at source by this seat on `origin/main`; the gate-exit-1 reading and the rule-1/rule-2 split are the dev's and are labelled as such.
